before.description: CapCut is a cross-platform video editor for mobile, desktop and web. The 2026 release is built around AI: describe-and-generate editing (AI Auto-Edit), the Seedream 5.0 text-to-image model, OmniHuman avatars and a generative effect engine, with the most advanced tools and 4K export reserved for paid plans.
before.description_long:
CapCut is a video editor from ByteDance that runs on iOS, Android, Windows, macOS and directly in the browser. It grew popular as a fast, approachable tool for short-form social video, and it still covers everything from quick TikTok clips to more layered multi-track projects.

The current 2026 version is a heavily AI-focused release. The headline additions are AI Auto-Edit, where you describe the video you want and CapCut assembles it; the Seedream 5.0 text-to-image model; OmniHuman digital avatars that generate a talking presenter; a generative effect engine with 50,000+ effects; plus Long-Video-to-Shorts and AI script and text-to-speech tools.

On the editing side you get a real multi-track timeline, keyframe animation, chroma key, auto-captions and a large library of templates, transitions, fonts and stock audio. The free tier is genuinely capable: multi-track editing, keyframes, chroma key, basic AI voiceover and 1080p export.

Pricing was restructured in 2025-2026. The free plan remains, and plain manual exports generally have no watermark, though Pro-locked templates and some AI-generated clips do add a CapCut mark. Paid tiers are Standard (about $9.99/month, mainly mobile, removes watermarks and unlocks more templates and fonts), Pro ($19.99/month or $179.99/year, adding 4K export, the full AI toolkit, more cloud storage and collaboration) and a Team plan starting around $24.99/month.

The main limitation is that the features people now come to CapCut for, the full AI suite, 4K export and the premium effects, sit behind Pro. Prices also vary by region and platform: App Store checkout can differ from the web price, and taxes or promos change the final figure. A student discount of roughly 50% on Pro has been reported.

CapCut suits creators who want quick, polished social video without a steep learning curve, and who are comfortable paying for Pro once they rely on the AI tools or need clean 4K output. If you only ever need simple 1080p edits, the free tier alone may be enough.

before.description: Webflow is a visual web development platform that has grown into an 'agentic web platform,' pairing its classic no-code designer with a standalone AI Site Builder that generates full multi-page sites from a single prompt.
before.description_long:
Webflow started as a visual builder that let designers produce production-grade HTML, CSS and JavaScript without writing code, backed by a built-in CMS and hosting. That manual designer is still the core, but the product has moved well beyond it.

As of July 2026 there are no numbered versions. The headline additions are a standalone AI Site Builder that generates a full multi-page site from a text prompt, plus a broader repositioning as an 'agentic web platform' — AEO (answer-engine optimization) agents, native AI-generated React components, and automatic AI localization.

On May 13, 2026 Webflow overhauled its plans. The old CMS and Business site plans were merged into a single Premium plan, Basic doubled its static-page allowance to 300, a high-end Team platform plan was introduced, and AI credits were folded into every Workspace tier, with quota enforcement starting June 29, 2026.

Pricing spans a free Starter site plan on a webflow.io subdomain, Basic at $15/mo yearly for a custom domain, and Premium at $25/mo yearly for the full CMS, code components and site search. E-commerce runs $29 to $212/mo, while platform plans go from Team at $2,500/mo up to a custom Enterprise quote. Workspace plans (Starter free, Core $19/mo, Growth $49/mo) bundle 200 to 400 AI credits, with a 2,000-credit add-on at $20/mo.

The main trade-offs are a steep learning curve for the visual designer, pricing that stacks up once you combine site and workspace plans, and AI credits that can run out on heavier use. It remains more designer-oriented than a simple template builder.

Webflow suits designers and agencies who want pixel-level control with clean exported code, teams that need a real CMS, and anyone wanting to spin up a first draft quickly with the AI Site Builder before refining it by hand.

Managed cloud adds Pro at $50/mo ($42.50/mo billed annually, $510/yr) and Max at $320/mo ($272/mo billed annually, $3,264/yr); a Team tier is coming soon. A separate pay-as-you-go credit wallet meters agent runs at an unpublished rate.

Limitations are worth noting. The platform is still officially beta, autonomous agents can burn credits or API tokens unpredictably, and the pay-as-you-go run pricing is not published up front. Self-hosting removes the subscription cost but shifts setup, LLM keys, and maintenance onto you.

AutoGPT suits developers and technical teams who want to build multi-step autonomous agents visually, publish or reuse agents from a store, and choose between free self-hosting and a managed cloud with predictable subscriptions.

before.description_long:
Claude is a conversational AI assistant from Anthropic, used through the web app, mobile apps, and the API. It handles long-form writing, analysis, coding, document reading, and multi-step reasoning, with an emphasis on careful, steerable responses.

The lineup has moved well past the earlier Claude 3 / Sonnet era. The most capable widely released model is now Claude Fable 5, generally available since June 9, 2026. The current family also includes Claude Opus 5 for complex agentic coding and enterprise work, Claude Sonnet 5 (released June 30, 2026), and the lighter Claude Haiku 4.5. A separate Claude Mythos 5 exists but is invitation-only through Project Glasswing.

The biggest practical change is context: current models offer a 1M-token context window rather than the older 200K, so you can load large codebases, long documents, or entire transcripts in a single conversation. The models also cover multimodal input and tool use across the product.

Pricing is tiered. The Free plan is $0. Pro is $20/month, or $17/month billed annually ($200/year). Max ranges from $100/month (5x usage) up to $200/month (20x usage). Team offers a Standard seat at $25/month ($20 annual) and a Premium seat at $125/month ($100 annual), with a five-seat minimum. Enterprise is custom, starting around $20/seat plus usage. API list pricing per million tokens is $10/$50 for Fable 5, $5/$25 for Opus 5, $3/$15 for Sonnet 5 (with a $2/$10 intro rate through Aug 31, 2026), and $1/$5 for Haiku 4.5.

Limitations are worth noting. Free and even paid plans have usage caps that reset on a rolling basis, so heavy users can hit limits mid-session. The most capable models are the most expensive on the API, and the top-end Mythos 5 is not openly available. As with any LLM, outputs still need checking for factual accuracy.

Claude suits writers, developers, analysts, and teams who want strong reasoning, large-context handling, and a choice of models to balance cost against capability.

The main limitation is exactly that metering: heavy AI users can burn through credits quickly, and the daily cap on the free tier makes sustained experimentation hard. Output quality from Make and First Draft is a starting point, not a finished design, and still needs a designer's hand.

Figma AI makes the most sense for teams already living in Figma who want AI woven into their existing files rather than a separate tool. If you rarely touch AI, the free allotment is fine; if AI is central to your workflow, budget for a paid tier and possible overage.

The current line is Stable Diffusion 3.5 (Large 8.1B, Large Turbo, and Medium 2.5B), free to self-host under the Community License for anyone under $1M in annual revenue, with a paid hosted API for teams that prefer not to run it themselves.
before.description_long:
Stable Diffusion is a family of open-weights image generation models from Stability AI. Unlike closed services, you can download the weights and run them on your own hardware, which is why it became the default base for a huge ecosystem of fine-tunes, LoRAs, ControlNets and local UIs.

The current release is Stable Diffusion 3.5, which ships in three variants: Large at 8.1B parameters, Large Turbo for fast few-step generation, and Medium at 2.5B for lighter machines. SD 3.5 is the most widely installed open image model by sheer install count, but it is no longer the quality leader among open weights — that position now belongs to Black Forest Labs' FLUX.2 as of 2026.

Capabilities cover text-to-image generation, prompt adherence and typography that improved over SDXL, and a broad toolchain for control and editing thanks to the open-model community. Related open models include SDXL Turbo, Stable Audio and Stable Fast 3D.

On pricing, self-hosting the open weights is free under the Stability AI Community License for individuals and organizations under $1M in annual revenue. Above that threshold an Enterprise License with custom pricing is required. Stability also offers a hosted route through the Developer Platform API (platform.stability.ai) with pay-per-credit billing: 1 credit is roughly $0.01, Stable Image Ultra runs about $0.08 per image and Stable Image Core about $0.03, with credit packs around $10 per 1,000 credits. A roughly $20/month membership tier has also been referenced by third parties.

The main limitations are practical. Running the larger models locally needs a capable GPU, results usually require prompt work and post-processing, and the revenue-gated license means larger companies cannot treat it as simply free. Quality at the top end now trails FLUX.2.

Stable Diffusion is the right choice if you want local control, an open pipeline you can fine-tune, and no per-image cost at small scale — and you are comfortable trading absolute peak quality for openness and flexibility.

before.description: Whisper is OpenAI's open-source speech-to-text model for transcription and translation. The latest open checkpoint is large-v3-turbo, a distilled version that runs roughly 8x faster than large-v3 with only a small accuracy trade-off.
before.description_long:
Whisper is a family of open-source speech recognition models released by OpenAI. It transcribes spoken audio into text and can translate speech from many languages directly into English. The weights are published under the permissive MIT license, so you can download them and run them on your own hardware.

The current open release is large-v3-turbo, a distilled model introduced in October 2024. It keeps almost all of the accuracy of the full large-v3 model while running about 8x faster, which makes it far more practical for batch jobs and near-real-time use. The full large-v3 checkpoint is still available when you want the highest possible quality.

Alongside the open models, OpenAI now offers hosted transcription through its API. The classic endpoint is whisper-1, and it has since been joined by GPT-4o-based models: gpt-4o-transcribe and the cheaper gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, which add options like speaker diarization. According to reports, a streaming variant, gpt-realtime-whisper, arrived around May 2026 and returns transcript deltas live as you speak.

Pricing splits into two tracks. The open-source models are free: you pay only for your own compute. The hosted API is usage-based: whisper-1 and gpt-4o-transcribe are $0.006 per minute ($0.36/hr), gpt-4o-mini-transcribe is $0.003 per minute ($0.18/hr), and the live gpt-realtime-whisper runs about $0.017 per minute.

Accuracy varies a lot by language. Whisper was trained on around 99 languages, but the quality is strongest for high-resource languages like English and drops noticeably for less common ones. Running the larger models locally also needs a capable GPU, and the model can occasionally hallucinate text during long silences.

Whisper is a good fit if you want a free, self-hostable transcription engine, need broad multilingual coverage, or want a managed API without building your own pipeline. Choose the hosted GPT-4o models if you need diarization or live streaming out of the box.
